header.goal: 470 paid orders (520 for October, prorated to 28 of 31 days)

fact_sheet.fact: Paid orders were 304 against a target of 470 (65%).
fact_sheet.source: GA4 purchases, paid channels; target 470 for October prorated to 28 of 31 days

fact_sheet.fact: Paid orders were 509 in the 28 days before, so the change is -40.3%.
Last year the same weeks fell 16.0% (468 to 393 paid orders).
On 2026-10-05 the Shopping daily budget went from $250 to $150, changed from the store's own login, after the founder asked for it on 2026-10-02 for cash flow.
fact_sheet.source: Google Ads change history (change_event) and agency notes

fact_sheet.fact: In the full weeks after the change, Shopping showed for 51% of eligible searches and lost 30% to budget, up from 4% before.
fact_sheet.source: Google Ads Shopping campaign by week

fact_sheet.fact: GA4 recorded 0 paid orders on 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 while paid sessions held at 783 over the two days.
fact_sheet.source: GA4 daily paid sessions and purchases

fact_sheet.fact: Meta orders went -5.7% on -2.0% spend, with frequency 1.8 to 1.9; no Meta changes in the window.
fact_sheet.source: Meta ad account insights and account activity

fact_sheet.fact: Non-brand search cost per order went from $30 to $35, with orders -14.9%.
Shopping's extra return per extra dollar, with the season removed, is 4.6 ($27 per extra order), against an average of 5.26 at the lower budget.
fact_sheet.source: computed from F3 and the Shopping weekly rows
fact_sheet.window: 4 weeks before vs 2 clean weeks after the change

fact_sheet.fact: The gap of 166 orders splits into about 88 from the budget change, 22 unrecorded on the tracking days, 43 from the season and 13 of normal swing.
A 14-day test at $250 a day costs $1,397 more, for an estimated 51 extra orders (ceiling 54) and about $6,400 in sales.
The purchase tag was reinstalled on 2026-10-16 07:40, and recorded purchases have been checked against paid sessions every morning since.
fact_sheet.source: agency notes pasted by the user

fact_sheet.fact: Shopping orders in Google Ads went from 344 to 191 (-44.5%).

causes.why: Logged change on a known day, and the budget-limited share jumped the same week in the same campaign.
causes.how_sized: (4-week average before x 0.84 season ratio, minus the 2 clean weeks after) = 25.7 orders a week, x 24 days after the change / 7

causes.cause: Purchase tag dropped after the checkout app update
causes.why: Sessions normal, purchases zero, and the store's developer confirmed the tag was missing and reinstalled it.
causes.how_sized: the paid conversion rate of the 7 days either side (2.83%) x 783 paid sessions on the two days. These orders probably happened but were not recorded; the store's order export can confirm.

causes.why: Last year's same weeks fell by a similar share, but nothing in this year's data can separate season from other demand changes.
causes.how_sized: the target minus the seasonal path: the prior 509 orders x 0.84 = 427, and 470 - 427 = 43

causes.why: Meta orders fell 5.7%, much less than the 16.0% seasonal fall, with steady frequency and no changes.
Spend was flat and orders fell 14.9%, close to last year's 16.0% seasonal fall, and the only change was 12 negative keywords on 2026-10-13.

parts.part: Unrecorded orders on 2 tracking days (confirmed, estimate)
Season the target did not allow for (likely)

gap_bridge.seasonal_path: With no budget change and no tracking gap, last year's 16.0% fall applied to the prior 509 orders gives about 427, so the target sat 43 orders above the seasonal path.
gap_bridge.normal_swing_rule: A remainder within 5% of the target (23.5 orders) is reported as normal swing, not as a cause.

budget_case.ask: Restore $100 a day ($150 back to $250) for a 14-day test
budget_case.ceiling_rule: budget-limited share / share shown (0.3 / 0.51) x 6.64 orders a day x 14 days = 54.7
budget_case.gate: Ask allowed: marginal ROAS 4.6 is at or above the 4.0 target and 30% of impressions are lost to budget (10% or more needed).
budget_case.stop_rule: If Shopping returns less than 4.0 over the 14 days, the budget goes back to $150 on day 15.
budget_case.caveat: An estimate from 6 weeks of one campaign. The season ratio comes from last year and may not repeat.

messages.type: missed target update with a budget request
messages.subject: October: 304 paid orders vs 470, and one budget decision
messages.body:
Hi {first name},

October paid orders came in at 304, 65% of the 470 we planned for these 28 days.

Two things we can prove explain most of the gap. The lower Shopping budget we agreed for October cash flow cost about 88 orders. A checkout update removed the purchase tag on Oct 14 and 15, so about 22 orders went unrecorded. The tag was back by the morning of Oct 16, and we now check orders daily. Most of the rest is likely the season: the same weeks fell 16% last year, more than our plan allowed for.

Each extra $1 on Shopping still returns about $4.60. Can we restore $250 a day for 14 days? That is $1,397 more, for an estimated 51 orders. If it returns under $4, it goes back on day 15.

A yes or no by Tuesday, Nov 3 lets us start Wednesday.

October paid orders: 304 vs 470 target (GA4, Oct 1 to 28). Two confirmed causes: Shopping budget at $150/day since Oct 5 (budget-limited share 4% to 30%, about 88 orders) and the purchase tag missing Oct 14 to 15 (783 paid sessions, 0 purchases recorded, about 22 orders). Meta and non-brand search moved with the season or better. One ask: could you send the store's order export for Oct 14 and 15 by Monday? It tells us how many of those 22 were real sales.

items.say: 304 paid orders against 470. Here is where the 166 went: about 88 from the lower Shopping budget, about 22 unrecorded on two tracking days, about 43 from a season our plan underestimated, and 13 that is normal swing.

The checkout update on Oct 14 removed the purchase tag. It was back on the morning of Oct 16. We now check recorded orders against sessions every morning. The order export tells us how many of the 22 were real.

At $150 a day Shopping misses 30% of the searches it could show on. Each extra dollar returns about $4.60. A 14-day test at $250 costs $1,397 more, for an estimated 51 orders and about $6,400 in sales, with a stop at under $4.
Last year these weeks fell 16%, and our October plan assumed less. We suggest setting the November target from last year's November change rather than from October's run rate.
Read back each decision, who owns it and the date.

likely_questions.q: Is the agency to blame for the drop?
likely_questions.a: Neither side alone. The budget change was agreed on Oct 2 for cash flow, and the tag loss came with a checkout update. We should have caught the tag in hours, not two days, which is why the daily check now exists.

likely_questions.q: Why not cut Meta instead of Shopping?
likely_questions.a: Meta orders fell 5.7%, Shopping orders fell 44.5% after the budget change, and the season took 16% last year. Meta is holding up best right now.

likely_questions.q: Will restoring the budget get us back to target?
likely_questions.a: No promise. The estimate is 51 extra orders over 14 days, and the most the missed searches could bring is about 54. The stop rule caps the downside at $1,397.
